title: AB routing weight-decay miscalculation caused split-serve, capacity surge, and rollback pinlock
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: During a staged AB rollout for a new decoding change, the routing controller applied an incorrectly implemented weight-decay function across replicas. The bug produced slightly different computed weights on nodes with different epoch timings, which resulted in a 60/40 split being interpreted as 40/60 in one AZ and 60/40 in another. This led to traffic concentration on the B variant in eu-west-1, saturating a subset of dedicated GPU pools and causing elevated latency and token requeueing. An automated rollback was initiated but failed to complete due to a version pin held by a live canary session and a pin-unpin race in the rollout controller. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause analysis, mitigations performed, and concrete action items to prevent recurrence.

root_cause: A logic error in the routing controller's weight-decay algorithm used for gradual traffic adjustments. The algorithm used a floating-point decay factor but accumulated weights with different event ordering across replicas, and rounding to micro-floats produced non-deterministic differences per node. Those differences, magnified by a per-AZ hashing variance, produced divergent effective splits. Additionally, the rollout controller allowed a pin to remain active during automated rollback, and the force-unpin path lacked sufficient guardrails causing the rollback to stall until manual unlock.
mitigations: Immediate: Forced unpin of canary sessions and completed rollback to stable model variant
Immediate: Redispatched in-flight requests to fallback pool to reduce saturation on dedicated eu-west-1 GPUs
Short-term: Increased autoscaler headroom for affected pools and temporarily raised queue depth thresholds to avoid cascading retries
action_items: ENG: Replace floating-point decay with deterministic fixed-point arithmetic for routing weights; add cross-node checksum validation (owner: Arjun Patel, due: 2026-03-20)
ENG/Infra: Implement a pre-rollback pin-unpin safety check that can force-unpin only after verifying no active long-lived sessions (owner: Lena Ortiz, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG: Add unit + e2e tests that simulate epoch drift across replicas and assert identical weight computation (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2026-03-17)
ENG/Observability: Dashboard and alerting rule: per-AZ effective-split drift metric and a high-priority PagerDuty alert when drift > 5% (owner: Carlos Rivera, due: 2026-03-15)
PM: Update rollout playbook to include explicit pin-unlock checklist and escalation path (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-19)
ENG/SRE: Introduce a soft-circuit-breaker that throttles new canary traffic to variants with >75% utilization until autoscaler scales up (owner: SRE Team, due: 2026-04-01)
Security: Audit pin/unpin API permissions to ensure only appropriate service principals can force-unpin (owner: Jordan Blake, due: 2026-03-25)
postmortem_summary: The incident was caused by a subtle non-determinism in how routing weights were computed across replicas combined with an operational exposure in the pin/unpin path. The customer-visible effect was elevated latency and retries in one region due to traffic concentration on a canary variant. Rollback semantics worked but were delayed by a lingering pin; manual intervention restored normal service. The fixes require both code changes (deterministic arithmetic, tests) and procedural changes (playbook updates, observability).
